title: T.R. in the Badlands
meta_description: In 1883 a bespectacled New York assemblyman got off a train in Dakota Territory to hunt buffalo. He left three years later a cattleman.

title: The Making of a Boy
meta_description: Asthma nearly killed him. A bedroom museum, a taxidermy tutor, and a father who told him to make his body.
social_image_alt: Theodore Roosevelt as a small boy, about two years old

title: The Youngest Man in the Assembly
meta_description: Elected at twenty-three, dismissed as a dude, and fighting the machine within a year. Fifteen questions on Roosevelt's first taste of power.
social_image_alt: The New York State Assembly, 1882-1884

title: Fifteen Years to the White House
meta_description: Civil service reformer, police commissioner, governor, vice president — and then Buffalo. Fifteen questions on the climb.
social_image_alt: Theodore Roosevelt as Assistant Secretary of the Navy

title: The Rough Riders
meta_description: A volunteer cavalry regiment of cowboys, Ivy League athletes, and lawmen, raised in weeks. Fifteen questions on 1898.
social_image_alt: Roosevelt and the Rough Riders on the captured hill

title: The Square Deal
meta_description: Forty-two years old and suddenly president. Trusts, coal strikes, a canal, and a Nobel Prize. Fifteen questions on eight years.
social_image_alt: Theodore Roosevelt in his private office

title: Two Hundred and Thirty Million Acres
meta_description: Parks, forests, monuments, bird reserves — the legacy that outlasted everything else he did. Fifteen questions on what he saved.
social_image_alt: Theodore Roosevelt and John Muir on Glacier Point, Yosemite

title: After the White House
meta_description: An African safari, a third-party crusade, a bullet in the chest, and an unmapped river in the Amazon. Fifteen questions on his last decade.
social_image_alt: Roosevelt and Carl Akeley on the African expedition

title: The People Around Him
meta_description: Edith, John Muir, Booker T. Washington, and the rivals who sharpened him. Fifteen questions on the company he kept.
social_image_alt: Portrait of Edith Kermit Carow Roosevelt

title: Life at Sagamore Hill
meta_description: Six children, a pony in the White House lift, and a family tree that reaches Eleanor and Franklin. Fifteen questions on the Roosevelts at home.
social_image_alt: Roosevelt family portrait

title: The Strenuous Life
meta_description: Boxing, judo, point-to-point walks through anything in the way. Fifteen questions on a creed he practised before he preached it.
social_image_alt: Theodore Roosevelt mounted in ranch clothes

title: The Naturalist
meta_description: A boy who mounted his own specimens grew into a president who could out-argue ornithologists. Fifteen questions on Roosevelt and the natural world.
social_image_alt: Roosevelt reading in front of his tent in camp

title: Where History Happened
meta_description: A Manhattan townhouse, a Badlands cabin, a hill above Oyster Bay, and the White House he renamed. Fifteen questions on the places that kept him.
social_image_alt: Roosevelt's birthplace at 28 East 20th Street

title: The Author President
meta_description: Some thirty-five books and thousands of articles, most of them written after living the story first. Fifteen questions on Roosevelt in print.
social_image_alt: The library at Sagamore Hill

title: Fact or Fiction
meta_description: He hated being called Teddy, and that is the least of it. Fifteen questions separating the famous stories from the record.
social_image_alt: Berryman's 1902 cartoon that started the teddy bear

title: The Measure of the Man
meta_description: Mount Rushmore, presidential rankings, and a name on a national park. Fifteen questions on how America decided to remember him.
social_image_alt: The Fraser equestrian statue at the Roosevelt Memorial

title: The Teddy Bear
meta_description: A president refused a shot he thought unsporting, a cartoonist drew it, and a Brooklyn shopkeeper wrote for permission to use the name.
social_image_alt: Berryman's 1902 cartoon "Drawing the line in Mississippi"

title: The White House Menagerie
meta_description: A badger named after the boy who caught it, a snake named after a thin aunt, and a pony that took the passenger lift. Twelve questions on the Roosevelt animals.
social_image_alt: Archie Roosevelt with Josiah, his pet badger

title: The Twenty-Seventh of October
meta_description: Born on 27 October 1858 and married on the same date twenty-two years later. One birthday he spent walking the grounds with a bullet in his chest.
social_image_alt: Theodore Roosevelt as a small boy, about two years old

title: Christmas at the Roosevelts'
meta_description: The president who protected 230 million acres had reservations about cutting an evergreen. His nine-year-old son smuggled one into a closet anyway.
social_image_alt: President Roosevelt seated between his sons Archie and Quentin, 1904

title: Eight Thousand Handshakes
meta_description: Every New Year's Day the White House opened its doors and anyone willing to queue could shake the president's hand.
social_image_alt: Members of the public filing in to the White House for the New Year's reception

title: The Dickinson Oration
meta_description: In 1886 a twenty-seven-year-old New York ranchman rode a freight train thirty-five miles to give a Fourth of July speech in a Dakota town six years old.
social_image_alt: Dickinson, Dakota Territory, in 1883

title: The Roosevelts at War
meta_description: Four sons in France and Mesopotamia, a father refused the division he begged for, and a telegram that never came.
social_image_alt: Quentin Roosevelt with his Nieuport aircraft

title: Greatheart
meta_description: The nights his father drove him through the streets to force air into his lungs, the substitute he hired in 1861, and the verdict his son never revised.
social_image_alt: Portrait of Theodore Roosevelt Sr. hanging at Sagamore Hill, photographed in 1966

title: The Path Between the Seas
meta_description: A French failure, a revolution that lasted a day, a doctor who fought mosquitoes, and the biggest earth-moving job ever attempted.
social_image_alt: A Bucyrus steam shovel working the Culebra Cut

title: The River of Doubt
meta_description: An unmapped Amazon tributary, a Brazilian co-commander, a drowning, a murder, and an infected leg a thousand miles from help.
social_image_alt: Roosevelt and Candido Rondon on the Brazilian expedition

title: Sixteen Battleships
meta_description: He had money to send them halfway and dared Congress to leave them there. Fourteen questions on the cruise that took the American navy round the world.
social_image_alt: The battle fleet leaving Hampton Roads

title: The Body He Made
meta_description: Asthma, a warning about his heart, a blind eye nobody knew about, a bullet that stayed in, and fevers that came back until the end.
social_image_alt: The 1912 X-ray plate showing the bullet in Roosevelt's chest

title: The Peacemaker
meta_description: Two empires at war, a navy yard in Maine, a buffet lunch that solved an unsolvable protocol problem, and the first Nobel Prize ever won by an American.
social_image_alt: The Russian and Japanese envoys with Roosevelt aboard the Mayflower
